q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT T.CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) CPC FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) T JOIN (SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) PC FROM PRODUCT) T2 WHERE PC = CPC

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products purchased by any customer is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if there exists at least one customer who has purchased all distinct products in the database.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with 2 products and 2 customers, where customer 1 has purchased both products, and customer 2 has purchased only one product.
